name: AI and agentic systems
owns: systems that read instructions and decide: LLM applications, retrieval, tool use, MCP servers, agent browsers, and the model supply chain
why_in_D: These systems have no parser to violate, no schema to bypass and no memory bounds to overrun. They fail differently: they can be convinced. A text instruction from a web page, a tool description, or a retrieved document can change what the system does, and there is no type system that separates data from command. That makes this the newest and least solved lens in the set.

factors.name: instruction and data separation
factors.def: whether the system architecturally distinguishes instructions from content it reads
factors.observable: behaviour changed by text arriving as data rather than as a prompt

factors.name: prompt injection persistence across turns
factors.def: whether injected text survives into later context and changes later decisions
factors.observable: an influenced action several turns after the injection

factors.name: indirect injection through retrieved content
factors.def: whether a document the model reads can carry an instruction
factors.observable: an action triggered by a retrieved document

factors.name: injection through tool output
factors.def: whether a tool's return value is trusted as instruction
factors.observable: a new goal adopted from a tool response

factors.name: cross tenant retrieval leakage
factors.def: whether retrieval respects tenant or principal boundaries per chunk
factors.observable: a document belonging to another tenant in context

factors.name: retrieval poison via write path
factors.def: whether an unattended write into the index can be retrieved later as trusted knowledge
factors.observable: attacker text returned as an authoritative source

factors.name: embedding inversion
factors.def: whether stored embeddings can be inverted back toward original text
factors.observable: reconstruction of content from vector similarity

factors.name: context window eviction behaviour
factors.def: whether safety instructions can be evicted by filling the window
factors.observable: a guard rail failing after long input

factors.name: many shot jailbreak response
factors.def: whether a long run of shaped examples shifts behaviour without an explicit request
factors.observable: disallowed output produced by pattern rather than instruction

factors.name: encoding based filter bypass
factors.def: whether the guard inspects decoded text or the raw form
factors.observable: a payload that passes as base64, escaped or transliterated

factors.name: multilingual guard coverage
factors.def: whether safety behaviour holds in every supported language
factors.observable: a disallowed output in a lower resourced language

factors.name: tool description trust

factors.observable: agent behaviour changed by description text alone

factors.name: tool parameter schema enforcement

factors.name: tool result authority

factors.name: tool selection confusion

factors.name: MCP server authentication
factors.def: whether a server authenticates its client and whether the client verifies the server
factors.observable: a connection established without mutual verification

factors.name: MCP transport exposure
factors.def: whether a server listens on a network interface it should not
factors.observable: a server reachable from another host

factors.name: MCP resource and prompt definition trust

factors.name: agent authority breadth

factors.name: agent to agent message authentication

factors.name: shared memory poisoning

factors.name: browser agent visual injection

factors.name: agent package installation authority

factors.name: output handling by the consuming application

factors.name: model output used in a query

factors.observable: a query built from model output

factors.name: link and citation following

factors.name: exfiltration through markdown images

factors.name: training data membership

factors.name: fine tune data boundary

factors.name: model file deserialisation

factors.observable: code execution on model load

factors.name: model source provenance

factors.name: backdoor trigger in a supplied model

factors.name: human in the loop quality

factors.name: rag freshness versus revocation

factors.name: model deprecation and forced migration

factors.observable: a version bump with no evaluation
